questions.text: Bancassurance refers to:
options: Banks offering insurance as corporate agents
Banks providing loans for premium payment
questions.explanation: Bancassurance is the distribution of insurance products through banks acting as corporate agents.

questions.text: Which of the following diseases are now mandatorily covered under health insurance?
questions.explanation: Recent IRDAI regulations mandate inclusion of mental illnesses and genetic disorders in health insurance coverage.

questions.text: Which intermediary represents the client and can work with multiple insurance companies?
questions.explanation: A direct insurance broker represents clients and can deal with multiple insurers across life, general, and health business.

questions.text: Subrogation allows the insurer to:
options: Step into the shoes of the insured to recover loss from third parties
questions.explanation: Subrogation enables the insurer to pursue recovery from third parties after compensating the insured.

questions.text: Health insurance claims become non-contestable after how many continuous years of premium payment?
questions.explanation: A moratorium period of 5 continuous years applies after which health insurance claims cannot be contested except for fraud.

questions.text: Which concept represents the present value of future income available to dependents?
questions.explanation: Human Life Value (HLV) is the present value of future income expected to support dependents.

questions.text: The typical range of returns from traditional endowment policies is around:
questions.explanation: Traditional endowment policies typically yield about 3–5% per annum based on official illustrations.

questions.text: Which is the most important criterion in evaluating a life insurance policy?
questions.explanation: The primary purpose of life insurance is protection; adequacy of cover comes before investment benefits.

questions.text: Which of the following is an advantage of ULIPs over mutual funds?
options: Free fund switches between asset classes without tax implications
questions.explanation: ULIPs allow fund switches within the same insurer without incurring tax or exit load.

questions.text: Whole life insurance covers the insured:
options: For their entire life or up to an upper age limit
questions.explanation: Whole life insurance provides cover for the insured’s entire lifetime or till the insurer’s specified maximum age.

questions.text: A general principle for global coverage of defined benefit policies (like life or accidental death) is that they:
options: Usually pay even if the insured event occurs outside India
Pay only if death occurs in India
questions.explanation: Defined benefit policies can usually be honoured globally as it is easier to verify the occurrence of the insured event.

questions.text: Most standard health insurance policies in India cover expenses:
options: Incurred in India only, unless otherwise specified
questions.explanation: Being indemnity policies, health plans typically restrict coverage to expenses incurred within India.

questions.text: Health insurance is best described as:
options: Indemnity policy reimbursing actual hospitalisation expenses
questions.explanation: Health insurance reimburses actual expenses up to the sum insured, making it an indemnity policy.

questions.text: A common cost-effective strategy for higher health cover is:
options: Buying many small base policies from different insurers
Combining a base health plan with a super top-up plan
Relying only on critical illness cover
questions.explanation: A base plan plus super top-up offers large cover at relatively low incremental premium.

questions.text: Critical illness insurance is best described as:
options: An indemnity policy that reimburses hospital bills
A defined benefit policy that pays lump sum on diagnosis of specified illnesses
A rider available only with motor policies
A compulsory cover under health plans
questions.explanation: Critical illness cover pays a fixed lump sum on diagnosis of listed illnesses, usually after a survival period.

questions.text: Retirement expenses are generally NOT the same as pre-retirement expenses because:
options: Some expenses fall while others like medical and leisure may rise
Housing costs always disappear at retirement
questions.explanation: Loan EMIs, work-related costs may fall, but medical, travel and recreation often rise; tax may change as income changes.

questions.text: To mitigate sequence risk, retirees can:
options: Maintain cash buffer for near-term expenses
questions.explanation: Keeping a buffer of liquid assets prevents forced withdrawals during market downturns.

questions.text: Sequence of returns risk refers to:
options: Order of returns affecting long-term corpus sustainability
Order of fund selection by investor
questions.explanation: Negative returns early in retirement can damage sustainability even if average returns remain similar.

questions.text: In the retirement planning framework, the years from retirement till the end of life are called:
questions.explanation: The distribution period is when the accumulated corpus is used to generate income for the retired life.

questions.text: Why is it risky to keep postponing retirement planning in favour of other goals?
options: Tax benefits on retirement products may be withdrawn
Accumulation period reduces, requiring much higher savings later
Retirement age is fixed by law
Inflation does not affect retirement expenses
questions.explanation: Delaying planning reduces years available for compounding, forcing very high later savings to reach the same corpus.

questions.text: Which factor most directly increases the corpus needed for retirement?
options: Higher expected inflation during and before retirement
questions.explanation: Higher inflation raises the future cost of living and therefore increases the corpus needed to fund retirement expenses.

questions.text: The maximum tax-free gratuity limit under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 is:
questions.explanation: The maximum tax-free gratuity amount is ₹20 lakh.

questions.text: The National Pension System (NPS) is regulated by:
questions.explanation: NPS is regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).

questions.text: On death of borrower in reverse mortgage, heirs can:
questions.explanation: Heirs can repay the outstanding amount to reclaim ownership of the property.

questions.text: Voluntary Provident Fund (VPF) refers to:
options: Employee’s voluntary contribution beyond the mandatory 12%
questions.explanation: Employees can contribute more than the statutory 12% as VPF; it earns the same interest as EPF.

questions.text: Post Office Monthly Income Scheme (POMIS) provides:
options: Monthly income through fixed interest payouts
questions.explanation: POMIS provides fixed monthly interest income for 5 years.

questions.text: Liquidity in a retirement portfolio is essential to handle:
questions.explanation: Liquidity helps meet unexpected expenses without disturbing income assets.

questions.text: Philanthropy discussions help advisers:
options: Strengthen client relationships through value alignment
questions.explanation: Talking about values deepens trust and long-term adviser–client engagement.

questions.text: In the pre-retirement phase, the focus should be on products that:
options: Generate fixed income with low growth
Allow growth through market participation despite some risk
questions.explanation: During accumulation, higher risk tolerance allows for equity or market-linked growth products.

questions.text: For retirees above 75 years, which factor becomes most important?
questions.explanation: In later life, focus shifts to capital safety, liquidity, and legacy planning.

questions.text: Which risk arises if a person withdraws EPF funds early before retirement?
options: Shortfall risk due to loss of compounding
questions.explanation: Premature withdrawals break compounding and reduce the corpus available for retirement.

questions.text: The primary role of an investment adviser in retirement planning is to:
options: Understand client goals and design strategies for steady post-retirement income
File tax returns on behalf of the client
questions.explanation: An investment adviser aligns client goals, risk tolerance, and timelines to ensure steady and sustainable post-retirement income.

questions.text: Stepping up investments during accumulation years helps because:
options: It compensates for early low contributions and rising income
questions.explanation: Increasing contributions as income rises helps harness compounding and meet corpus goals efficiently.

questions.text: Which section defines the residential status of an individual?
questions.explanation: Section 6 of the Income Tax Act defines and governs residential status determination.

questions.text: In India, the financial year runs from:
questions.explanation: India’s financial year runs from April 1 to March 31 for income and tax computation.

questions.text: The period of holding for bonus shares is reckoned from:
options: Date of purchase of original shares
Date of allotment of bonus shares
Date of issue of rights offer
questions.explanation: For bonus shares, period of holding starts from the date of allotment.

questions.text: Redemption of Sovereign Gold Bonds by individuals is:
options: Not regarded as transfer and exempt
questions.explanation: Redemption of Sovereign Gold Bonds by individuals is not regarded as transfer and hence not taxable as capital gains.

questions.text: Which of these incomes is specifically included under 'Income from Other Sources'?
options: Winnings from lotteries or online games
questions.explanation: Winnings from lotteries, crossword puzzles, and online games are always taxed under 'Income from Other Sources'.

questions.text: Income from interest on government securities is taxable under:
questions.explanation: Interest on government securities is taxable under 'Income from Other Sources' unless forming part of business income.

questions.text: Long-term capital gains on other mutual funds (held >24 months) are taxed at:
questions.explanation: Long-term capital gains on mutual funds are taxed at 12.5% under new regime.

questions.text: Which of the following is a Government Security with less than one-year maturity?
questions.explanation: Treasury Bills are short-term government debt instruments with maturity below one year.

questions.text: Short-term capital gains on equity-oriented mutual funds are taxed at:
questions.explanation: Short-term gains on equity-oriented MFs with STT payment are taxed at 20%.

questions.text: Equity investments primarily generate income from:
questions.explanation: Equity investors earn through dividend distributions and capital gains when shares appreciate in value.

questions.text: Under Section 111A, short-term capital gains on listed REIT units with STT are taxed at:
questions.explanation: Short-term capital gains on listed REIT/InvIT units where STT is paid are taxed at 20% plus surcharge and cess.

questions.text: Winding up of a mutual fund scheme is treated as:
questions.explanation: When mutual funds are wound up, proceeds received by investors are treated as redemption of units, attracting capital gains tax.

questions.text: A Will must be signed by the testator in the presence of how many witnesses?
questions.explanation: A valid will must be signed in the presence of two witnesses who attest to the signature.

questions.text: When a will is destroyed intentionally by the testator, it results in:
questions.explanation: A will can be revoked by intentional destruction or by making a new one.

questions.text: When a person dies without a will, it is termed as:
questions.explanation: When no will exists, the person is said to have died intestate and property distribution follows succession laws.

questions.text: Who is eligible to be appointed as a legal guardian for minors?
options: Court-appointed person or as specified in a Will
questions.explanation: Guardians are either court-appointed or designated under a valid will for minor dependents.

questions.text: Estate planning documents should be reviewed:
options: Every 5 years or on major life events
questions.explanation: Wills and estate plans should be updated every few years or after major life changes.

questions.text: What is ‘Probate’?
options: A certificate issued to validate a Will
questions.explanation: Probate is a legal process validating the authenticity of a Will.

questions.text: Joint holding of assets allows:
options: Simpler access to assets after one holder’s death
questions.explanation: Joint holdings simplify access to assets after the death of one holder, based on mode of operation.

questions.text: What is the purpose of asset protection strategies?
questions.explanation: Asset protection aims to safeguard personal or business assets from creditor claims.

questions.text: Who can make a nomination?
questions.explanation: Only individuals can make nominations, not firms or institutions.

questions.text: A Will should ideally be reviewed:
options: Every 2–3 years or after major life events
Once created, it need not be changed
questions.explanation: Reviewing a Will every few years ensures it reflects current assets and family situations.

questions.text: What is the primary benefit of creating a trust for minor children?
options: Ensuring controlled use of funds until maturity
questions.explanation: Trusts can manage assets for minors until they reach a defined age.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a tool used during a person’s lifetime for estate planning?
questions.explanation: Nomination becomes effective after death, unlike other tools which are used during lifetime.

questions.text: Which of the following anomalies is most persistent in markets?
questions.explanation: Momentum effect—where past winners continue to perform—persists longer due to behavioural biases.

questions.text: According to Benjamin Graham, in the short run, the market is:
questions.explanation: Graham said, 'In the short run, the market is a voting machine; in the long run, a weighing machine.'

questions.text: Overconfidence and self-attribution biases often lead investors to:
questions.explanation: Overconfidence combined with self-attribution leads to overtrading and poor diversification.

questions.text: The best way to manage retail therapy behaviour is to:
options: Open a separate budgeted account for such expenses
questions.explanation: Creating a small budgeted account helps contain overspending due to emotional impulses.

questions.text: Buying insurance only for tax saving is an example of:
questions.explanation: It reflects a bias where decisions are driven by short-term tax benefits rather than true protection needs.

questions.text: A client insisting on funding her child’s education over retirement demonstrates:
questions.explanation: The client prioritizes emotionally charged goals; the adviser must help rebalance priorities objectively.

questions.text: Aggressive investors are most likely to:
options: Take active exposure to equities and growth assets
questions.explanation: Aggressive investors are experienced and willing to accept higher volatility for long-term gains.

questions.text: Which of the following describes a conservative investor?
options: Prefers low risk and steady returns
Willing to take high risk for short-term gains
questions.explanation: Conservative investors prioritize capital protection and stable income over high returns.

questions.text: Which SEBI regulation mandates risk profiling by investment advisers?
questions.explanation: Regulation 16 of SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013 mandates risk profiling to ensure product suitability.

questions.text: A model portfolio helps advisers by:
options: Providing identical portfolios to all clients
Customizing recommendations based on client profile
questions.explanation: Model portfolios act as templates that can be customized based on each client’s unique circumstances.

questions.text: Risk profiling involves assessing which three factors?
options: Ability, Willingness, and Need to take risk
Tax rate, Portfolio value, and Tenure
questions.explanation: Risk profiling considers ability (financial capacity), willingness (psychological comfort), and need (goal requirement).

questions.text: Diversification works best when asset classes have:
questions.explanation: Low or negative correlation among asset classes ensures smoother portfolio performance.

questions.text: A valid risk profiling questionnaire should be:
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates that questionnaires should be simple, objective, and unbiased to ensure reliability.

questions.text: An investor near retirement should ideally have:
options: Balanced mix with higher debt allocation
questions.explanation: Retirees prioritize safety and income stability, so debt-heavy portfolios suit them better.

questions.text: Dynamic Asset Allocation uses:
options: Pre-defined models and valuation triggers for automatic rebalancing
questions.explanation: Dynamic asset allocation relies on pre-set models or valuation metrics to trigger portfolio rebalancing.

questions.text: Moderate investors generally:
options: Understand risk is necessary for long-term goals
questions.explanation: Moderate investors balance risk and return and understand that some risk is essential for long-term wealth.

questions.text: Asset allocation primarily aims to:
questions.explanation: Asset allocation spreads risk across asset classes to stabilize returns and minimize loss exposure.

questions.text: Strategic allocation is reviewed primarily when:
questions.explanation: Strategic allocation is long-term and revised mainly when fundamental changes occur in investor profile.

questions.text: Strategic Asset Allocation is based on:
options: Long-term goals and investor’s risk profile
questions.explanation: Strategic asset allocation aligns long-term goals, time horizon, and risk tolerance.

questions.text: Which of the following factors increases risk appetite?
questions.explanation: With more earning members, income stability improves, leading to higher risk tolerance.

questions.text: Minimum investment amount for a Portfolio Management Service (PMS) is:
questions.explanation: As per SEBI norms, the minimum investment in PMS is ₹50 lakh.

questions.text: ULIPs issued after February 1, 2021 lose Section 10(10D) exemption if annual premium exceeds:
questions.explanation: ULIPs with premiums above ₹2.5 lakh per year no longer qualify for tax exemption under Section 10(10D).

questions.text: Fixed Maturity Plans (FMPs) are similar to:
questions.explanation: FMPs are closed-ended debt mutual funds with fixed tenure, often compared to FDs.

questions.text: Which form of gold investment does NOT attract GST?
questions.explanation: Sovereign Gold Bonds are paper-based and exempt from GST.

questions.text: Category III Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) require a minimum investment of:
questions.explanation: AIF Category III has a minimum entry threshold of ₹1 crore per investor.

questions.text: REITs primarily invest in:
options: Infrastructure projects like bridges and roads
Commercial real estate generating rental income
questions.explanation: REITs (Real Estate Investment Trusts) mainly invest in income-generating commercial properties.

questions.text: In comparison of debt instruments, liquidity is highest in:
questions.explanation: Bank FDs offer instant liquidity, albeit with penalties for premature withdrawal.

questions.text: Sovereign Gold Bonds provide what annual interest rate?
questions.explanation: Sovereign Gold Bonds earn 2.5% interest per annum, paid semi-annually.

questions.text: Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) differ from Index Funds because:
options: They are sold only by AMCs
They are traded on stock exchanges like shares
They are only available for debt instruments
questions.explanation: ETFs are listed and traded on exchanges, unlike index funds which are transacted at NAV with AMCs.

questions.text: In National Pension System (NPS) Tier 1, what percentage of corpus can be withdrawn tax-free at age 60?
questions.explanation: At retirement, 60% of NPS corpus can be withdrawn tax-free; 40% must be used to buy an annuity.

questions.text: What is the lock-in period for investments in PPF?
questions.explanation: PPF has a lock-in of 15 years, with partial withdrawals allowed after 5 years.

questions.text: Which of the following offers exposure to infrastructure assets?
questions.explanation: Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) invest in infrastructure projects like roads, ports, and power plants.

questions.text: Between Company Deposits and Debentures, which is riskier?
questions.explanation: Company deposits are unsecured, whereas debentures are usually secured; hence deposits carry higher risk.

questions.case_text: A retiree, Mrs. D’Souza, is offered two investment choices by her adviser: (A) A product that ‘guarantees’ she will not lose money, but with low return; (B) A balanced fund that may fluctuate but has better long-term return prospects. She chooses the guaranteed option because she fears any possibility of loss.

questions.text: Mrs. D’Souza’s preference for avoiding losses even at the cost of lower returns is an example of:
questions.explanation: Loss aversion is the tendency to prefer avoiding losses more strongly than acquiring equivalent gains.

questions.text: Her adviser presents option A emphasizing ‘no loss’ and option B emphasizing ‘possible loss’, which is an example of:
questions.explanation: How choices are framed (in terms of gains or losses) can influence decisions even when underlying outcomes are similar.

questions.text: What is the RISK of her choice if inflation is higher than her guaranteed return?
options: Erosion of real purchasing power over time
questions.explanation: If nominal returns are below inflation, her real wealth and purchasing power will decline gradually.

questions.text: Which approach better balances her fear and need for growth?
options: Mix of guaranteed products with some exposure to balanced funds
questions.explanation: A combination ensures she has a safe base while some assets aim to protect against inflation over the long term.

questions.text: What is an adviser’s responsibility in this situation?
options: Explain trade-offs between safety and growth in simple terms
questions.explanation: Advisers must help clients understand both the comfort and long-term consequences of their risk choices.

questions.case_text: Rohan, 38, is returning to India after working abroad for 10 years. He has accumulated foreign currency deposits, a 401(k)-type retirement account overseas, and mutual funds in India invested as an NRI. He plans to settle in India permanently with his spouse and two young children. He wants a comprehensive plan covering residential status, tax, asset allocation, and long-term goals such as children’s education and retirement.

questions.text: On returning permanently, Rohan’s RESIDENTIAL status for Indian tax purposes will depend on:
options: Number of days stayed in India in the relevant previous year and preceding years
questions.explanation: Indian tax residency is determined primarily by physical presence as per Income-tax Act rules, not by citizenship or account type. Day-count tests decide whether he becomes resident, resident but not ordinarily resident, or NRI.

questions.text: Why is it important to review his OVERSEAS retirement accounts and investments?
options: To understand tax implications, withdrawal rules and currency risks as he shifts his base to India
questions.explanation: Different countries have their own tax rules and penalties for withdrawals. Rohan must plan the timing and method of accessing these funds and consider currency risk relative to his rupee-based expenses.

questions.text: His NRI investments in Indian mutual funds and NRE deposits need to be reviewed because:
options: They may have to be redesignated as resident accounts when his status changes
questions.explanation: On change of residential status, bank and investment accounts must be updated (e.g., NRE to resident or RFC) to comply with FEMA and banking regulations. This may affect tax treatment and repatriation.

questions.text: For long-term goals in India, his asset allocation should primarily be:
options: Balanced across rupee assets like equity, debt and real estate aligned to goals and risk profile
questions.explanation: Since his future expenses (education, retirement) will be largely in rupees, the core of his portfolio should be in Indian assets suited to his goals and risk capacity, with any foreign exposure used thoughtfully for diversification.

questions.text: What is the FINANCIAL PLANNER’s key role in this situation?
options: Coordinating a holistic plan covering tax, FEMA compliance, risk management and investment strategy in consultation with specialists
questions.explanation: The planner provides an integrated roadmap, while working with tax and legal experts in both jurisdictions to ensure compliance, optimization and alignment with the family’s life goals.

questions.case_text: A case study for training: A mid-career couple with two children has multiple goals, EMI obligations, some investments, and inadequate insurance. The adviser is expected to use Excel to project cash flows, retirement corpus and education funding, and then suggest an implementable plan.

questions.text: Which Excel FUNCTION is most commonly used to compute EMI for a loan?
questions.explanation: The PMT function calculates the periodic payment for a loan given interest rate, tenure and present value.

questions.text: To compute FUTURE VALUE of a lump sum invested today at a fixed rate, which function is appropriate?
questions.explanation: The FV function in Excel calculates future value of a single sum or annuity based on given rate and periods.

questions.text: To determine the corpus needed today to meet a series of future expenses, which Excel function is used?
questions.explanation: PV gives the present value of future cash flows discounted at a particular rate.

questions.text: Using Excel models in financial planning mainly helps to:
options: Quantify assumptions and test different scenarios systematically
questions.explanation: Excel allows planners to project cash flows under various assumptions, improving clarity and decision-making.

questions.text: After creating an Excel-based plan, the adviser should:
options: Explain assumptions, limitations and action steps clearly to clients
Use it only for internal purposes
questions.explanation: Clients must understand the basis of recommendations and the steps needed to implement and monitor the plan.

questions.case_text: The Sharma family has reached out to a financial planner because they feel trapped in debt. They have a home loan EMI of ₹35,000, car loan EMI of ₹12,000 and outstanding credit card dues with minimum payments of ₹10,000 per month. Their combined monthly income is ₹1,20,000 and expenses (excluding EMIs) are ₹55,000. They have almost no emergency fund and minimal investments. They want a comprehensive plan to get out of the debt cycle and start investing for the future.

questions.text: What is their TOTAL monthly EMI and minimum payment burden?
questions.explanation: Total monthly outgo on loans and card dues = 35,000 (home) + 12,000 (car) + 10,000 (card) = ₹57,000.

questions.text: What is their DEBT-SERVICING RATIO (EMIs as % of income) approximately?
questions.explanation: Debt servicing ratio ≈ 57,000 ÷ 1,20,000 ≈ 47%. This is high and leaves limited room to manage emergencies or start meaningful investments.

questions.text: Which debt should typically be TARGETED FIRST for repayment?
options: Credit card dues with highest interest rate
questions.explanation: Credit card debt usually carries the highest interest rate and compounds quickly. Accelerating repayment of such high-cost debt is crucial to breaking the debt cycle.

questions.text: What should be the FIRST priority in their financial plan alongside debt restructuring?
options: Building at least a small emergency fund while cutting discretionary spending
questions.explanation: Even while repaying debt, setting aside a basic emergency buffer (even one month’s expenses to start with) reduces the risk of further borrowing when unexpected expenses arise. This should go hand-in-hand with strict expense control.

questions.text: Once high-cost debt is under control, how should investments be introduced?
options: Suddenly invest all surplus into a single product
Start with systematic investments (SIPs) aligned to goals and risk profile, gradually increasing as their balance sheet improves
Avoid investing and keep all money in cash
questions.explanation: A gradual, goal-linked SIP approach builds discipline and wealth over time. Investments should be introduced after stabilizing cash flows, creating emergency fund, and securing adequate insurance, not before.

questions.case_text: Deepak, 35, wants to retire at 60. His current monthly expenses are ₹60,000. He expects inflation at 6% p.a. and post-retirement portfolio return at 8% p.a. He wants to provide for 25 years in retirement. He currently has no separate retirement corpus but can invest ₹25,000 per month towards retirement.

questions.text: What is Deepak’s CURRENT annual expense level?
questions.explanation: Annual expenses = 60,000 × 12 = ₹7,20,000? However exam-style rounding may treat 60,000 × 12 as 7.2 lakh, but the option closest to typical demonstration is ₹7,20,000. (Use the option that matches 60,000 × 12).

questions.text: Roughly how many years are left for his retirement planning?
questions.explanation: Deepak is 35 and wants to retire at 60, so he has 25 years to accumulate his retirement corpus.

questions.text: If inflation is 6%, his annual expenses at retirement (start of age 60) will be approximately how many times today’s expenses?
questions.explanation: Over 25 years at 6%, (1.06)^25 is roughly 4.29; however exam-style approximations often round this closer to 4x. Students are expected to recognize that expenses more than triple or quadruple due to inflation.

questions.text: Which of the following is the BEST way to estimate the retirement corpus required?
options: Taking current income and multiplying by 5
Inflating expenses to retirement and then discounting over retirement years at real rate
Ignoring inflation and using current expenses
questions.explanation: Proper retirement planning inflates current expenses to retirement date and then discounts over the retirement period using real return (post-inflation).

questions.text: What type of asset allocation is MOST suitable for Deepak during his accumulation phase?
questions.explanation: With a 25-year horizon, growth assets like equity should dominate the portfolio, supported by some debt for stability.

questions.case_text: Mr. Shah, a salaried individual, has salary income, interest income from bank fixed deposits and dividend income from equity mutual funds. He also has capital gains from sale of listed shares. He wants to understand how different incomes are taxed and how to plan his investments tax-efficiently.

questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE about SALARY income?
options: It is taxed at special rates
It is taxed at slab rates applicable to the individual
questions.explanation: Salary is taxed at normal slab rates after considering applicable exemptions and deductions.

questions.text: Interest on bank fixed deposits is generally taxed as:
options: Income from other sources at slab rates
questions.explanation: FD interest is classified as income from other sources and taxed at slab rates applicable to the individual.

questions.text: Dividends from domestic equity mutual funds are generally:
options: Taxable in the hands of investors as per current rules
questions.explanation: Under recent changes, dividends are taxable in the hands of the recipient investor at applicable slab rates.

questions.text: Capital gains from sale of listed equity shares are classified as:
questions.explanation: Profits from sale of capital assets like shares are classified as capital gains and taxed based on holding period and type.

questions.text: Which tax-saving approach is MOST suitable for Mr. Shah?
options: Investing in ELSS, NPS and using Section 80C deductions appropriately
questions.explanation: Legal tax planning through eligible deductions (like 80C, 80CCD) and tax-efficient products such as ELSS and NPS is advisable.
